approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

referral_steps.text: Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(1); § 1060.5(a)).
Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Planning Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(2)).

Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Department of Building Inspection for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(3)). It has applied in this form since 14 January 2024 (Ord. 250-23, File No. 230861).
Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Department of Public Health for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(4)).
Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Fire Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(5)).
Limited Live Performance Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2.1(b)).

Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2.2(b)).
Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound Permit application: this application is sent to the Planning Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2.2(b)).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Most directly comparable: amended a prior CUA to add amplified live entertainment and extend hours to 1:30 a.m. at 1337–39 Grant Ave (44 meters away), same North Beach NCD zoning, same corridor as subject site. This is an intensification of entertainment use in an existing food/drink business.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved amplified live entertainment with extended hours until 1:30 a.m. (past midnight) in a CUA amendment in 2012 at a restaurant/POE on the same block of Grant Avenue. This is a use decision showing that intensification of entertainment hours and amplification were approved on this corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 1994 to add live entertainment to an existing bar at 1363–71 Grant Ave (64 meters away), same North Beach NCD, same street corridor. Like the subject concept, this added entertainment to a bar already operating.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved adding live entertainment to an existing bar ('Grant and Green bar') on this same block of Grant Avenue in the North Beach NCD via conditional use authorization. This is a use decision establishing that bars on this corridor can obtain CUA approval to add entertainment.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 2009 to add live entertainment (DJs and live music) to an existing wine bar at 460 Columbus Ave (120 meters away), North Beach NCD. Demonstrates Planning approval for amplified entertainment (DJs) added to a bar.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved adding DJs and live music to an existing wine bar in North Beach NCD, showing willingness to approve amplified entertainment added to a bar use via conditional use authorization. This is a use decision.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA amendment approved in 2010 to add amplified music to a prior entertainment authorization at 408–414 Columbus Ave (85 meters away), North Beach NCD. Parallel to the subject concept's request to intensify entertainment with amplification.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved a CUA amendment to add amplified music to a venue that already had a Place of Entertainment permit in the North Beach NCD. This is a use decision showing that amplification can be added via amendment to an existing entertainment approval.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Miscellaneous permit approved in 2000 for a change of hours for a bar/place of entertainment at 1371 Grant Ave (64 meters away), North Beach NCD, referencing prior CUA 1993.255C. Shows the same bar from 1993.255C obtained approval to modify operating hours.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This is an agency referral (not a Commission use decision) approving a change of hours for the Grant and Green bar that received its original entertainment CUA in 1993.255C. It confirms that hour changes for entertainment in bars on this block have been approved, though as an agency referral it carries less weight than a Commission decision.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA application to expand an existing bar into basement space at 1345 Grant Ave (53 meters away), North Beach NCD, withdrawn in 2018 after 4 months. Only withdrawal found among bar intensification cases on this corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Applicant withdrew a CUA to expand a bar's physical footprint at 1345 Grant (same block, 53 meters away). The record does not state why it was withdrawn. This is a use decision showing that physical expansion (not just hour/entertainment intensification) triggered a CUA requirement and was not pursued to decision.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approved in 2001 for non-amplified live entertainment at 1326–29 Grant Ave (the subject property), citing the 1994 CUA for live entertainment at this address. Directly on-point for the subject site's entertainment history.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved non-amplified live entertainment at 1326 Grant Ave in 2001 under a 1994 CUA (Motion 13769). This is an agency referral, not a Commission decision, but it establishes that the subject site has had entertainment approval since at least 1994, limited to non-amplified performance.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Miscellaneous permit denied in 2001 for a Place of Entertainment at 1268 Grant Ave (47 meters away), North Beach NCD. The only denial in the candidate set, providing a cautionary data point.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply within 30 days of starting business in San Francisco. The fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27, each plus a $4 state fee). Every other city department asks for your BAN, so do this immediately after forming the entity and getting the EIN. The registration year runs April 1 to March 31 and renewal is due by the last day of February each year.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with San Francisco Planning whether intensification of entertainment and hours without physical expansion requires a new Conditional Use Authorization or can proceed under the 1994 CUA.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Planning Information Center (pic@sfgov.org) or schedule a pre-application meeting with a planner assigned to the North Beach area. Explain that 1326 Grant Ave is an existing bar with a 1994 CUA (Motion 13769) for non-amplified live entertainment, and you propose to add amplified sound and extend entertainment hours past midnight without enlarging the space. Ask: (1) Does Planning Code § 780.3(c)(1)(A) permit this as intensification without a new CUA, or does § 178 require a new CUA because a conditional use is being significantly altered? (2) If a new CUA is required, can it be processed as an amendment to Motion 13769 or must it be a new case? Request a written response or a Property Information Map report and Letter of Determination. filing_playbook.action: Obtain music licensing (ASCAP and BMI) and complete RBS training for all alcohol servers and managers.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Federal copyright law requires a blanket public performance license to play music (background, DJs, live covers, TV with music). Annual fees are formula-based on occupancy and music use (typically $300–$2,500 per catalog). Most venues need both ASCAP and BMI because their catalogs do not overlap. California AB 1221 requires Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) certification for every alcohol server and their managers within 60 days of hire. Register on the ABC RBS Portal ($3), complete an approved course (about $10–$25), and pass the exam. Keep the certification list on site for ABC inspections. These are fast (1–7 days each).

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost range cover the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000), the Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days, $2,708), and the health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470), which are the approvals in the entitlement path. These are times to approval for cases that are granted; denied or withdrawn cases are not included in this range. The CUA is the critical path: pre-application meeting, environmental review, community meeting, 300-foot mailed notice, 30-day posted notice, and Planning Commission hearing, followed by a 30-day appeal period, typically take six to ten months when approved. The Entertainment Commission permit follows the CUA and adds two to four months (intake meeting, referrals to five departments, 30-day posted notice, and Commission hearing). The health permit is administrative and takes two to six weeks after the CUA is approved. The cost does not include the ABC license because the description does not state whether the existing Type 48 license will be transferred, amended, or remain unchanged, so no ABC cost is included. If a Type 48 transfer is needed, add 90–180 days and $17,000–$450,000 (license purchase price plus transfer fees). The cost also does not include business registration ($55–$700), entity formation ($70–$150), a fictitious business name ($60–$120), workers' compensation insurance (premiums are a percentage of payroll, not a government fee), music licensing ($600–$5,000 for ASCAP and BMI combined), or RBS training ($13–$150 for five employees), because these are not discretionary approvals and are required for any bar. The timeline assumes no discretionary review, no neighborhood appeal to the Board of Supervisors, and no revisions required by the Entertainment Commission; protests or appeals can add three to six months.

records_summary: 1326 Grant Ave has operated as a bar since at least 1999 with an active Type 48 (full-liquor bar) license issued January 2024. The property sits in the North Beach NCD where bars are a conditional use on the first story, and the North Beach Special Use District permits intensification of an existing bar without a new Conditional Use Authorization if the space is not enlarged. The site history shows continuous bar use with multiple ownership changes approved as continuations (2006, 2010, 2023). The immediate block is heavily saturated: 56 food/drink businesses within 500 feet, 13 of them bars, and 45 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet (107 within 1,000 feet)—triggering an undue-concentration flag. Nearby precedent is limited but favorable: a 2012 CUA at 1337–39 Grant approved amplified live entertainment with extended hours to 1:30 a.m., and a 1994 CUA at the same block approved live entertainment in a café, though the base-rate count is too low (N=7 use decisions in 10 years) to show an approval rate.
